elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 7.2 reads: "Customer has no obligation to disclose or match for Vendor any commercial offer it receives, or to give Vendor most-favoured-customer terms." The original disclose-and-match obligation is removed in operative language, and Section 12.3 (retained) reinforces that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN existed to preserve.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no Customer-side MFN obligation exists anywhere in the rendered text (7.2 negates disclosure/matching and MFC terms; 12.3 confirms no MFC commitment), so there is no MFN whose product scope could exceed a defined product.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no surviving Customer MFN obligation in 7.2 or elsewhere, there is no duration to cap; the position is stricter than the 12-month fallback.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no comparison or matching mechanic remains after the deletion of the disclose-and-match sentence, so no carve-out is needed.

elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Recorded for completeness: the fallback level is satisfied a fortiori because the preferred no-MFN outcome is achieved in revised Section 7.2.

reasons: Original Section 7.2 ("Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives") was an MFN running in Vendor's favour with no product limit, no time limit and no like-for-like carve-outs — walk-away territory under the rule, so a redline was warranted and the 'deviation' classification is correct.

This is a disclose-and-match mechanic, correctly characterised as MFN rather than exclusivity: Customer remained free to engage other providers after compliance, and Section 12.3 expressly preserves that freedom. The finding therefore does not double-count an exclusivity issue.

Preferred level is complete: the operative replacement affirmatively negates any Customer duty to disclose, match, or grant most-favoured-customer terms, leaving no undefined trigger or promise deferred to the comment.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the single offending sentence in 7.2; no Vendor-granted MFN existed to preserve, no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural language was added, and no words outside the target element were removed. The tail "or to give Vendor most-favoured-customer terms" overlaps in substance with the Section 12.3 acknowledgment, but it restates the very element under review rather than adding an out-of-checklist requirement, so it does not defeat minimality; a pure deletion would have been marginally tighter.

Intent is preserved: Section 12.3 is left untouched and now reads consistently with 7.2 rather than contradicting it; no cross-reference, defined term, or commercial mechanic elsewhere depends on the deleted disclose-and-match duty.
